chunk_findings.detail: The change's stated goal is "one JSON shape for every list kind with `rows`", and it extends that shape to the refusal path in `ddflow/api/viewers.py`, which now emits `rows`, `total`, `shown`, `limit`, `truncated` and `filters`. But the other refusal path — the stray/unsupported-flag branch in `viewers_lists.py` (used e.g. by `ddflow --json list task --item T1`, the exact command the updated tests now exercise) — emits only `record_kind`, `reason`, `rows`, `total`, `shown`. It omits `limit`, `truncated` and `filters`, so the two refusal bodies are not the same `list@1` shape. A JSON consumer that always reads the uniform shape (e.g. reads `body["truncated"]` to decide whether to page, or `body["limit"]`) works after a viewer-level refusal such as `ddflow --json list task --phase P-nonexistent` but raises `KeyError` for `ddflow --json list task --item T1`. The `--json` refusal branch should build the same key set (or delegate to the same helper) as the `O.refused(..., rows=[], total=0, shown=0, limit=limit, truncated=False, filters={})` call added in `viewers.py`, otherwise the "one shape" guarantee is only half implemented.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/viewers_lists.py:185 (`emit_json` in the stray-flag branch)

chunk_findings.detail: The change claims to give "one JSON shape for every list kind", and it explicitly makes the two no-rows paths carry list metadata. But the two refusal paths now emit *different* key sets. In `ddflow/api/viewers.py` the `V.ViewError` refusal is extended with `rows=[]`, `total=0`, `shown=0`, **plus `limit`, `truncated` and `filters`** (mirroring the success payload, which is why those keys were added there at all). In this file the stray-flag refusal added only `rows`/`total`/`shown` and still omits `limit`, `truncated` and `filters`. So for input `ddflow --json list task --item T1` (a flag `task` does not take) the emitted body is `{"schema":"list@1","record_kind":"task","reason":"task has no --item","rows":[],"total":0,"shown":0}` — a caller that parses every list/refusal body uniformly, e.g. reads `body["limit"]` (or `body["filters"]`) as it can after any successful `--json list`, gets a `KeyError` on exactly this path. That is two JSON shapes, not one, for the same operation, and the omission is in the path this diff just touched.

chunk_findings.detail: The change registers `--all` for *every* list kind (`_list_flags` appends `Param("all", ...)` with no `kind` guard) and the new help text says `"accepted for every kind; this kind lists all its rows already"`, but the selector whitelist that the list path validates against (`_TAKES`, whose comment is "any other one that is set is refused") was only extended for `task`, `phase` and `research` (plus the pre-existing `bug`/`lesson`). `session` and `search` are still `{"id"}` and `{"query","mode","sources","source","phase"}`. So `ddflow list session --all` (or `list search --all`) parses the flag now, forwards `all=True`, and is refused by the validator — the exact opposite of the advertised "one command line works for any kind", and a regression relative to the substring of the help the author just wrote. If `all` is meant to be a harmless no-op for kinds that do not narrow, `_TAKES` needs `all` for `session`/`search` too; otherwise the fallback help text must not claim universal acceptance.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/viewers.py:85 (`_TAKES`) / ddflow/surfaces/commands/viewers_lists.py:66 (`Param("all", ...)`)

chunk_findings.detail: This call invokes `empty_list(a.kind)` with only the kind, so the refusal payload always carries `limit` = `V.DEFAULT_LIMIT`. The sibling refusal in `view_list` uses `empty_list(kind, limit)` with the limit actually passed in, and the success payload reports the effective limit. So for `ddflow --json list task --phase P --limit 5 --item X` (a stray flag that hits the surface refusal) the JSON says `"limit": <V.DEFAULT_LIMIT>` while the equivalent API refusal says `5`; the "one shape for every list kind" parity the change is built on holds for key names but not for the `limit` value. `a.limit` (or `R.LIST_DEFAULT_LIMIT`) is available here, so the value should be forwarded.

chunk_findings.detail: This call invokes `empty_list(a.kind)` with only the kind, so the refusal payload always carries `limit` = `V.DEFAULT_LIMIT`. The sibling refusal in `view_list` uses `empty_list(kind, limit)` with the limit actually passed in, and the success payload reports the effective limit. So for `ddflow --json list task --phase P --limit 5 --item X` (a stray flag that hits the surface refusal) the JSON says `"limit": <V.DEFAULT_LIMIT>` while the equivalent API refusal says `5`; the "one shape for every list kind" parity the change is built on holds for key names but not for the `limit` value. `a.limit` (or `R.LIST_DEFAULT_LIMIT`) is available here, so the value should be forwarded.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/viewers_lists.py:186 (`emit_json({**empty_list(a.kind), "reason": reason})`)

chunk_findings.detail: The change's stated goal is that the two refusal paths now carry the *same* list shape by sharing `api.empty_list`, and the API-side path does preserve the caller's limit: `O.refused("view.list", str(exc), **empty_list(kind, limit))` (`ddflow/api/viewers.py`) forwards the `limit` argument that was actually requested. The surfaces-side path does not: `emit_json({**empty_list(a.kind), "reason": reason})` calls `empty_list` without the second argument, so it always stamps `V.DEFAULT_LIMIT` and `truncated: false` regardless of what the user asked for. Reproduction: `ddflow --json list task --item T1 --limit 5` lands in this branch (`item` is not in `_TAKES["task"]`, which is exactly the probe the earlier review used) and emits `"limit": 20` (the default) even though the request set `--limit 5`; the sibling view refusal for the same arguments would emit `"limit": 5`. A client that trusts `limit`/`truncated` from the refusal payload gets metadata that was never applied, so the "one JSON shape" the change set out to establish still disagrees between the two refusal paths. The value is available as `a.limit`, so the branch should pass it (e.g. `empty_list(a.kind, a.limit)`).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/viewers_lists.py:185 (`emit_json` in the stray-flag branch)

data.summary: ddflow --json search ... --source bogus and ddflow --json session list --state bogus print no JSON body on refusal (view_head returns before emit_json), unlike list; stdout empty, rc 3. Fix: emit the body (now carrying rows: []) when --json before returning REFUSED in ddflow/surfaces/commands/viewers_search.py; regression test parses the stdout of both.
